test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 30 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the Attorney General of India?

options.text: He / She can participate in sessions of the parliament.
He / She can vote in the Lok Sabha during the passage of confidence motion and no - confidence motion.
He / She cannot participate in joint sitting of the parliament.
He / She does not enjoy any immunity or privileges as compared to members of the parliament.

solution:
The Correct answer is __**He / She can participate in sessions of the parliament.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Attorney General of India** is the highest law officer in India and is appointed under **Article 76 of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• He/She is responsible for advising the government on legal matters and representing the Union Government in the Supreme Court and other courts.
 
• The Attorney General has the **right to participate** in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament.
 
• However, while he/she can speak and participate in discussions in Parliament, the Attorney General does **not have voting rights** in parliamentary proceedings.
 
• The Attorney General enjoys certain privileges and immunities while performing their official duties but does not hold a seat in Parliament.
 
• This provision allows the Attorney General to contribute to legal discussions and ensure that the government is well-informed on constitutional and legal matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 2: He / She can vote in the Lok Sabha during the passage of confidence motion and no-confidence motion.**__

 __
 
• The Attorney General does **not have voting rights** in Parliament as he/she is not an elected member of either House.
 
• Voting rights are reserved for elected members of Parliament, such as MPs in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: He / She cannot participate in joint sitting of the parliament.**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect. The Attorney General has the **right to participate in all sessions** of Parliament, including joint sittings.
 
• However, as mentioned earlier, he/she cannot vote in these proceedings.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: He / She does not enjoy any immunity or privileges as compared to members of the parliament.**__
 
 
• The Attorney General enjoys certain **privileges and immunities** while discharging their official duties, similar to those granted to Members of Parliament.
 
• These include protection against legal proceedings for acts performed in their official capacity.
